explanation: Bridge: a carpenter uses a saw as a tool of his trade, and a tailor uses a needle as a tool of his. A crop is what a farmer produces, not his tool, and a hospital is a doctor's workplace.
Bridge: a petal is one part of a flower, and a page is one part of a book. A root grows in soil but is not part of the soil, and water is held in a glass (contents and container), not part of it.
Bridge: HOT is the opposite of COLD, and TALL is the opposite of SHORT. BIG and LARGE are synonyms, and WARM : HOT shows two degrees of the same quality rather than opposites.

Bridge: a drought can cause a famine, and a virus can cause an infection. FLOOD : RAIN has the order reversed, because rain causes a flood, not the other way round. A doctor brings about a cure as an agent, not as a natural cause.
Bridge: a puppy is a young dog, and a kitten is a young cat. A lamb is a young sheep but wool is its coat, not the adult animal; a den is where a cub lives, and a hen lays an egg.

Bridge: a thermometer is an instrument that measures temperature, and a barometer is an instrument that measures air pressure. A telescope is used to look at stars but does not measure a quantity, and a stethoscope is a doctor's tool, not something it measures.

Bridge: a whisper is a very soft use of the voice and a shout a very loud one, so the pair runs from low to high intensity; a drizzle is light rain and a downpour very heavy rain. LOUD and NOISY are near-synonyms with no change in degree, and SPEAK : LISTEN are two different actions.
Bridge: an author creates a book, and a composer creates a symphony. A reader only uses a magazine and does not make it, and a librarian works in a library rather than creating it.
Bridge: a sparrow is a type of bird, and a rose is a type of flower. FRUIT : MANGO has the order reversed (the category comes first), and a wing is a part of a bird, not a type of one.
Bridge: a pilot operates an aircraft, and a driver operates a bus. A passenger travels on a train without operating it, and a garage is only a mechanic's workplace.

PARSIMONIOUS means extremely unwilling to spend, so it is the opposite of GENEROUS. Bridge: verbose (using too many words) is the opposite of concise. OBSTINATE : STUBBORN and AFFLUENT : WEALTHY are synonym pairs, and something lavish is often expensive, which is not an opposite.
Bridge: a sheep is one member of a flock, and a soldier is one member of an army. A nest is a bird's home, not a group of birds, and honey and milk are things bees and cows produce.

Bridge: botany is the scientific study of plants, and astronomy is the scientific study of stars and space. A microscope is a tool used in biology and a laboratory is a place where chemistry is done, so neither is the subject studied.

Bridge: a brake is used to stop a vehicle, and a key is used to unlock something; each pair is an object and its function. A pen writes on paper, but paper is the surface, not the action, and a kitchen is only where an oven is kept.
Bridge: when you are hungry you eat to satisfy the need, and when you are thirsty you drink to satisfy it. Shouting may express anger but does not remove it, and working makes tiredness worse.

Bridge: an oasis is a small isolated area of water and greenery surrounded by desert, as an island is a piece of land surrounded by sea. Sand is the material a dune is made of, and a bridge crosses a river rather than being surrounded by it.

Bridge: a fever is a sign that an illness is present, and smoke is a sign that a fire is present. Wax is the material a candle is made from, not a sign of it, and an umbrella is protection against rain.
Bridge: ANCIENT is the opposite of MODERN, and VICTORY is the opposite of DEFEAT. BRAVE : COURAGEOUS and OLD : AGED are synonym pairs, so they show sameness, not opposition.

IMPECUNIOUS means having little or no money. Bridge: an impecunious person lacks money, and an ignorant person lacks knowledge. TALENTED : SKILL is the tempting trap, but a talented person has skill rather than lacking it; WEALTHY : PROPERTY is also a having relationship.
Bridge: a raisin is a dried grape, and a prune is a dried plum. A seed grows into a tree, which is development, not drying, and an orchard is where apples grow.
Bridge: a helmet is worn to protect the head, and a glove is worn to protect the hand. A ring is also worn on a part of the body, but as an ornament, not for protection.

Bridge: bread is the product made by a baker, and furniture is the product made by a carpenter; the product comes first. CARPENTER : FURNITURE has the right words in the wrong order, and a doctor treats a patient rather than making one.

Bridge: to adore is to like very strongly, and to loathe is to dislike very strongly; the first word is the more intense form of the second. LOVE : HATE are opposites, not two degrees of the same feeling.

Bridge: a frugal person avoids waste, and an honest person avoids deceit. PATIENT : WAIT is the closest trap, but a patient person is willing to wait, which is doing the action rather than avoiding it; a brave person has courage.

stem: Choose the pair with the same relationship as SEED : TREE
explanation: Bridge: a seed develops into a tree, and a bud develops into a flower. A branch is part of a full-grown tree, not an earlier stage of it, and a vase only holds a flower.
Bridge: a hive is the home in which bees live, and a stable is the shelter in which a horse lives. A pride is a group of lions, not their home, and a calf is a young cow.

Bridge: a cobbler repairs shoes, and a mechanic repairs cars; each pair is a worker and the thing he mends. Chalk is a teacher's tool and a kitchen is a chef's workplace, so neither is the object repaired.

Bridge: a miser is a person who typically hoards money, and a spendthrift is a person who typically squanders it. GLUTTON : STARVE is the trap: a glutton eats too much, so starving is the opposite of his typical action.

Bridge: a cup is a container that holds tea, and an envelope is a container that holds a letter. A kettle is placed on a stove but does not contain it, and a plate is kept in a kitchen rather than holding it.

Bridge: wool is the material a sweater is made from, and clay is the material a pot is made from. SHEEP : WOOL shows an animal and what it gives, not a material and the finished product, and a pot only holds soup.

Bridge: a centimetre is a unit for measuring length, and a kilogram is a unit for measuring mass. LITRE : WATER is the trap: a litre measures volume, and water is a substance, not a quantity. A ruler and a clock are instruments, not quantities.

Bridge: CANDID means the same as FRANK (open and honest), and LUCID means the same as CLEAR. TIMID : BOLD and DILIGENT : LAZY are opposites, and fragile describes glass rather than meaning the same thing.

Bridge: a philanthropist is a person marked by generosity, and an optimist is a person marked by hopefulness. A pessimist and a novice are marked by the lack of cheerfulness and expertise, and a tyrant demands obedience from others rather than showing it.
Bridge: summer comes straight after spring, and afternoon comes straight after morning; each pair is in sequence. SUMMER : HOT gives a season and its quality, and WEEK : DAY is a whole and its part.

Bridge: a painter works on a canvas as the surface for his work, and a writer writes on paper as the surface for his. FARMER : TRACTOR is the trap: a tractor is a tool or machine, not the surface worked on, and a song is what a singer produces.

Bridge: a doctor works in a hospital, and a teacher works in a school; each pair is a worker and the workplace. A recipe is what a chef follows and a verdict is what a judge gives, not places of work.

VORACIOUS means extremely hungry. Bridge: voracious is the extreme degree of hungry, as ecstatic is the extreme degree of happy. CONTENT : SATISFIED and TIMID : SHY are near-synonyms of the same strength, and FURIOUS : CALM are opposites.

Bridge: a vaccine is used to prevent a disease, and a seat belt is used to prevent injury. FIRE : SMOKE and EXERCISE : SWEAT show cause and effect, the opposite of prevention, and a pharmacy is where medicine is sold.
Bridge: moo is the sound a cow makes, and roar is the sound a lion makes. A tail is a part of a dog and a saddle is equipment for a horse, so neither is a sound.

Bridge: a stanza is one section of a poem, and a chapter is one section of a novel. POET : RHYME links a writer with a feature of his work, and a stage is where an actor performs, so neither is a section of a whole.

Bridge: to quench thirst is to satisfy it completely, and to satiate hunger is to satisfy it completely. PROVOKE : ANGER is the trap: provoking starts anger rather than ending it, and kindling likewise starts a fire.
Bridge: a teacher trains and instructs a student, and a coach trains and instructs an athlete. DOCTOR : MEDICINE links a person with something he prescribes, not someone he instructs.

Bridge: an illiterate person is unable to read, and a mute person is unable to speak. A tall person can reach easily, the opposite of inability, and a tired person needs sleep rather than being unable to do it.
Bridge: an archipelago is a group of islands, and a constellation is a group of stars. A peninsula is a single piece of land almost surrounded by water, not a group, and a volcano throws out lava.

Bridge: flour is the main ingredient from which bread is made, and milk is what butter is made from. An oven is the appliance a cake is baked in and a bakery is the shop where bread is sold, so neither is an ingredient.
Bridge: a feather is known for being light, and lead is known for being heavy; each pair is a thing and its typical quality. GLASS : WINDOW is a material and a product made from it, not a quality.

ERUDITE means having great knowledge. Bridge: a scholar is expected to be erudite, and an acrobat is expected to be agile. TIMID : LION and NOISY : LIBRARY are the opposite of what we expect of a lion and a library.
Bridge: the ear is the organ we use to hear, and the nose is the organ we use to smell. EYE : TEAR is the trap: a tear is something the eye produces, while the eye's function is to see.

Bridge: a preface is an introduction placed at the beginning of a book, and a prologue is an introduction placed at the beginning of a play. EPILOGUE : NOVEL is the trap, because an epilogue comes at the end, not the beginning.
Bridge: you trim hair to cut it shorter, and you mow grass to cut it shorter. Watering a flower helps it grow rather than cutting it, and a brush is the tool used to paint, not the thing acted on.

Bridge: a brush is the tool used by a painter, and a scalpel is the tool used by a surgeon; the tool comes first. SURGEON : SCALPEL has the same words in the wrong order, so it does not match the pattern tool : user.
Bridge: a finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot. A glove covers the fingers and a sleeve covers the arm, so those pairs are coverings, not body parts within a whole.

OBDURATE means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind. Bridge: an obdurate person is unwilling to yield, and a reticent person is unwilling to speak. GARRULOUS : TALK is the trap: a garrulous person talks too much, the opposite of unwillingness, and a credulous person believes too readily.

Bridge: a camera is the device that produces a photograph, and a loom is the machine that produces cloth. ALBUM : PICTURE is the trap: an album only stores pictures and does not make them, and a lens is a part of a pair of glasses.

Bridge: a torrent is a strong, fast flow of water and a trickle a very weak one, so the pair goes from strong to weak; a gale is a very strong wind and a breeze a light one. RIVER : OCEAN goes the other way, from smaller to larger.
Bridge: a palace is the home in which a king lives, and a nest is the home in which a bird lives. A pilot flies in the sky but does not live there, and a fin is a part of a fish.

Bridge: a referee presides over a match and makes sure the rules are followed, and a judge presides over a trial in the same way. A player is a member of a team rather than its official, and a spectator only watches from a stadium.

ALLEVIATE means to make a problem less severe and AGGRAVATE means to make it worse, so they are opposites. Bridge: augment (increase) is the opposite of diminish (decrease). MITIGATE : EASE, EXACERBATE : WORSEN and PLACATE : SOOTHE are all synonym pairs.

Bridge: petrol is the energy source that powers a car, and electricity is the energy source that powers a fan. A wheel is a part of a bicycle, not its power, and a driver operates a taxi rather than powering it.
Bridge: GENTLE is the opposite of HARSH, and KIND is the opposite of CRUEL. GENTLE : MILD and HARSH : STRICT reuse words from the stem but are near-synonyms, and soft describes silk.

Bridge: an atlas is a book made up of a collection of maps, and an anthology is a book made up of a collection of poems. A globe is a model of the earth, not one item in a collection, and a compass shows direction.

Bridge: an orchestra is a group made up of musicians, and a team is a group made up of players; the group comes first. PLAYER : TEAM has the right words in the wrong order, and a band performs a song rather than being made of songs.

LACONIC means using very few words. Bridge: a laconic person uses few words, and an abstemious person takes little food and drink. VORACIOUS : FOOD is the trap with the opposite meaning, since a voracious eater takes a great deal, and VERBOSE also means using too many words.

Bridge: a car is kept and sheltered in a garage, and an aeroplane is kept and sheltered in a hangar. TRAIN : TRACK is the trap: a train runs on a track but is not stored in it, and a sail is part of a ship.
Bridge: twenty is double ten, and eight is double four. TEN : TWENTY uses the same numbers in the reverse order, giving half instead of double, and five : fifteen is a ratio of three.

Bridge: a medicine is taken to counter an illness, and an antidote is taken to counter a poison. SNAKE : VENOM is the trap: a snake produces venom rather than countering it, and a bottle only holds pills.

Bridge: a pedal is the part a rider pushes to move a bicycle forward, and an oar is what a rower pushes to move a boat forward. ANCHOR : SHIP is the trap: an anchor holds a ship still instead of moving it.

Bridge: a vacuum is the complete absence of matter, and darkness is the absence of light. BALLOON : AIR is the opposite, since a balloon is filled with air, and an ocean and a desert are full of water and sand.

CACOPHONY means a harsh, unpleasant mixture of sounds. Bridge: a cacophony is an unpleasant sound, and a stench is an unpleasant smell. FRAGRANCE : SMELL is the trap, but a fragrance is a pleasant smell, and an echo is simply a reflected sound.

A SYCOPHANT is a person who praises powerful people too much to gain favour. Bridge: a sycophant typically flatters, and a braggart typically boasts. A hermit avoids company, so socialising is the opposite of what he does, and an orator speaks rather than listens.
Bridge: books are kept in a library for the public to use, and paintings are kept in a gallery for the public to see. PAGE : CHAPTER is a part and a whole, and a shelf is made of wood.

Bridge: a draft is a rough early version of an essay, and a sketch is a rough early version of a painting. BRUSH : PORTRAIT is the trap: a brush is the tool used to make a portrait, not an earlier version of it.

Bridge: a proton carries a positive charge, and an electron carries a negative charge; each pair is a particle and its charge. NEUTRON : NUCLEUS gives a particle and where it is found, not its charge.
Bridge: a chick is the young of a hen, and a calf is the young of a cow. CUB : FOREST gives a young animal and where it lives, and an egg is laid in a nest.
Bridge: a watch is worn on the wrist, and a bangle is worn on the arm. A pocket and a lace are parts of a shirt and a shoe, not things worn on a part of the body.

Bridge: an egg hatches when new life breaks out of it, and a seed germinates when a new plant starts to grow from it. BOIL : WATER is a change in water, not the start of a new life, and a hen lays eggs rather than hatching.

Bridge: a dentist is a doctor who specialises in treating the teeth, and a cardiologist is a doctor who specialises in treating the heart. PHARMACIST : MEDICINE is the trap: a pharmacist prepares and gives out medicine but does not treat a part of the body.
Bridge: a broom is used to sweep, and a needle is used to sew; each pair is a tool and the action it performs. MOP : BUCKET pairs two cleaning items but gives no action.

A EULOGY is a speech full of praise, and a DIATRIBE is a bitter speech full of criticism. Bridge: a eulogy is a form of words that expresses praise, as a diatribe is one that expresses criticism. ELEGY : JOY fails because an elegy expresses sorrow, not joy, and a lullaby is sung to a child, which names the listener, not what is expressed.

Bridge: a whale belongs to the class of mammals even though it lives in water, and a penguin belongs to the class of birds even though it cannot fly. The other pairs are false: a dolphin is a mammal, a bat is a mammal and a frog is an amphibian.
Bridge: a lubricant reduces friction, and an anaesthetic reduces the feeling of pain. FERTILISER : GROWTH and FUEL : FIRE go the opposite way, because fertiliser and fuel increase what follows them.
Bridge: BEGIN and START mean the same thing, and FINISH and END mean the same thing. The other three pairs are opposites, not synonyms.

Bridge: a blizzard is a violent, overwhelming fall of snow, and a deluge is a violent, overwhelming fall of rain. HAIL : ICE is the trap: hail is simply made of ice and need not be extreme, and a drought is a lack of water.

INCORRIGIBLE means so bad that it cannot be corrected. Bridge: something incorrigible cannot be corrected, and something illegible cannot be read. EDIBLE : EAT and AUDIBLE : HEAR are the trap: they mean something can be eaten or heard, the opposite of the stem.
Bridge: sugar has a sweet taste, and a lemon has a sour taste. SALT : WHITE and CHILLI : GREEN give a colour, not a taste, and honey is made by a bee.

Bridge: a tremor is a small, mild version of an earthquake, and a hill is a small, low version of a mountain. LAKE : POND has the order reversed, going from larger to smaller, and ROCK : STONE are near-synonyms.
Bridge: bark is the outer covering of a tree, and peel is the outer covering of an orange. A seed is found inside an apple, not on its surface, and a root is the part of a plant below the ground.

Bridge: a novice is a beginner who may one day become an expert, and an apprentice is a learner who may one day become a master. TEACHER : PUPIL runs the other way, from the skilled person to the learner, and a veteran is already an experienced soldier.
Bridge: a herbivore is an animal that eats plants, and a carnivore is an animal that eats flesh. COW : MILK is the trap: a cow produces milk rather than eating it, and a jungle is where a lion lives.

A BIBLIOPHILE is a person who loves books, and a CINEPHILE is a person who loves films. Bridge: a bibliophile is a lover of books as a cinephile is a lover of films. MISANTHROPE : PEOPLE is the trap with the opposite meaning, because a misanthrope dislikes people.

ENERVATE means to drain of energy, so it is a synonym of WEAKEN (not of energise, a common mistake). Bridge: enervate means the same as weaken, and abate means the same as lessen. INVIGORATE : TIRE, AMELIORATE : WORSEN and ENRAGE : CALM are all opposite pairs.

Bridge: a chronological list is arranged according to time, and an alphabetical list is arranged according to letters. NUMERICAL : CALCULATOR and GEOGRAPHICAL : ATLAS name a tool or a book, not the thing used to set the order.

A PANACEA is a remedy believed to cure all ills. Bridge: a panacea works for every ill, as a master key opens every lock. ANTIDOTE : VENOM is the trap: an antidote cures one particular poison, not all of them.

Bridge: a rudder is used to steer a ship, and a steering wheel is used to steer a car. PROPELLER : AEROPLANE is the trap: a propeller drives an aircraft forward but does not steer it, and an anchor holds a boat in place.
Bridge: breakfast is the meal eaten in the morning, and dinner is the meal eaten in the evening. LUNCH : SANDWICH gives a meal and a food that may be eaten at it, not its time of day.

Bridge: a hammer is the tool used to drive in a nail, and a screwdriver is the tool used to turn in a screw. SAW : CARPENTER gives a tool and its user, not the object it acts on, and a spanner is kept in a toolbox.
Bridge: an obstacle hinders progress, and fog hinders visibility. FUEL : SPEED and LADDER : HEIGHT go the opposite way, because fuel and a ladder help someone gain speed or height.

Bridge: applause is a way of showing approval, and a frown is a way of showing displeasure. SMILE : MOUTH and TEAR : EYE give an expression and the part of the body involved, not the feeling it shows.

PIQUED means slightly annoyed, while FURIOUS means extremely angry. Bridge: piqued is a mild form of what furious is in the extreme, as apprehensive (slightly afraid) is a mild form of terrified. IRATE : ANGRY runs the wrong way, from the stronger word to the weaker, and CALM : SERENE are near-synonyms.

Bridge: a ticket gives a person the right to enter a cinema, and a boarding pass gives a person the right to board a flight. RECEIPT : PURCHASE is the trap: a receipt is proof of something already bought and gives no entry anywhere.
Bridge: scissors are used to cut, and a spoon is used to stir; each pair is a tool and the action it performs. KNIFE : BUTTER is the trap: butter is the thing a knife acts on, not an action.
Bridge: a roof is the top covering of a house, and a lid is the top covering of a box. A carpet is laid on a floor and paint is put on a wall, so those pairs are a surface and something added to it.
Bridge: LOUD is the opposite of QUIET, and RICH is the opposite of POOR. NOISY : LOUD and QUICK : FAST are synonym pairs, so they show sameness rather than opposition.

Bridge: a spider builds a web, and a beaver builds a dam; each pair is an animal and the structure it makes. FLY : WEB is the trap: a fly gets caught in a web but does not build it, and a feather grows on a bird.
Bridge: a kid is the young of a goat, and a foal is the young of a horse; the adult animal comes first. FOAL : HORSE has the right words in the wrong order, and a kennel is a dog's shelter.

Bridge: a shopkeeper provides a service to a customer, and a lawyer provides a service to a client. JUDGE : COURT gives a person and his workplace, and scissors are a tailor's tool, so neither names the person served.

Bridge: grass is typically green in colour, and coal is typically black in colour. FIRE : HOT, SUGAR : SWEET and RAIN : WET also give a typical quality, but it is temperature, taste or feel, not colour.

Bridge: an insulator blocks the flow of electricity, and a dam blocks the flow of water. WIRE : CURRENT and PIPE : GAS are the trap with the opposite idea, because a wire and a pipe carry the flow instead of stopping it.

OMNIPOTENT means having unlimited power, and OMNISCIENT means having unlimited knowledge. Bridge: an omnipotent being has all power, as an omniscient being has all knowledge. IGNORANT : KNOWLEDGE is the trap, because an ignorant person lacks knowledge.

Bridge: a stethoscope lets a doctor hear a heartbeat that is too faint to hear unaided, and a microscope lets a person see germs that are too small to see unaided. GLASSES : FRAME is a part of the object, not what it helps us sense.

Bridge: an umbrella protects a person from rain, and sunglasses protect the eyes from glare. BUCKET : WATER is the trap: a bucket holds water rather than protecting anyone from it, and wind lifts a kite.
Bridge: honey is produced by a bee, and silk is produced by a silkworm; the product comes first. WOOL : SWEATER is a material and something made from it, and milk is only stored in a bottle.

Bridge: a marathon is a long race and a sprint a short one, and a novel is a long work of fiction and a short story a short one. RACE : MEDAL gives an event and its prize, not a long and short form of the same thing.
Bridge: a joke causes laughter, and an insult causes anger. TEAR : SORROW is the trap: sorrow causes tears, so the cause and the effect are in the reverse order.

A SOPORIFIC is a drug or thing that causes sleep. Bridge: a soporific brings on sleep, as an anaesthetic brings on numbness. INSOMNIA : SLEEP is the trap: insomnia is the inability to sleep, the opposite of causing it.

Bridge: huge means extremely big, and tiny means extremely small; the second word is the stronger degree of the first. HUGE : BIG has the order reversed, and THIN : SLIM are near-synonyms of the same strength.
Bridge: a nurse looks after a patient, and a shepherd looks after sheep. WOLF : SHEEP is the trap: a wolf hunts sheep rather than caring for them, and a butcher cuts and sells meat.

MAGNANIMOUS means generous and forgiving, the opposite of PETTY. Bridge: magnanimous is the opposite of petty, as prodigal (wastefully extravagant) is the opposite of thrifty. AFFABLE : FRIENDLY, TACITURN : QUIET and HAUGHTY : PROUD are all synonym pairs.

Bridge: the moon revolves around the earth, and the earth revolves around the sun. SUN : EARTH has the order reversed, since the sun does not revolve around the earth, and stars are simply seen at night.
Bridge: a hexagon has six sides, and a triangle has three sides. A square has four sides and a pentagon five, so those pairs give the wrong number, and round describes a circle's shape.

Bridge: a wall is built up from many bricks, and a tiled floor is made up of many tiles; each pair is a unit and the structure it forms. PAINT : WALL is the trap: paint only coats a wall and is not one of the units it is made of.

An ICONOCLAST is a person who attacks established beliefs and traditions. Bridge: an iconoclast challenges tradition, as a rebel challenges authority. HISTORIAN : PAST is the trap: a historian studies the past rather than opposing it, and a follower supports a leader.
Bridge: a boat travels along a river, and a car travels along a road. TYRE : WHEEL is a part and a whole, and a pilot flies a plane rather than being the route it travels on.

Bridge: exhausted means extremely tired, and starving means extremely hungry; the stronger word comes first. HUNGRY : STARVING has the right words in the wrong order, and HAPPY : GLAD are near-synonyms of the same strength.

Bridge: a meteorologist is a scientist who studies the weather, and a seismologist is a scientist who studies earthquakes. GEOLOGIST : HAMMER gives a scientist and a tool, not the subject studied, and an astronaut travels in space rather than studying it as a subject.
